title: Early-refill share for Prescriptions & Renewals replacement counts, by financial class
content:
**Revenue cycle payer-class note — Prescriptions & Renewals replacement fills.**

When the lost supply behind a replacement fill is counted, the early-refill share used for this count follows the financial class recorded on the patient's billing account — the Patient Financial Account — on the day of the replacement: a Medicaid Managed Care Account uses 85 percent; a Medicare Advantage Account or a Medicare Part B Account uses 80 percent; a Commercial PPO/POS Account or a Commercial HMO/EPO Account uses 70 percent; any other financial class uses the early-refill percentage of the prescription's class.

| Financial class on the Patient Financial Account | Early-refill share for the count |
|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Account | 85 percent |
| Medicare Advantage Account | 80 percent |
| Medicare Part B Account | 80 percent |
| Commercial PPO/POS Account | 70 percent |
| Commercial HMO/EPO Account | 70 percent |
| any other financial class | the early-refill percentage of the prescription's class |

**Notes.**
- The financial class is read from the Patient Financial Account as recorded, not from the caller's description of the plan.
- For the last row, the percentage is the class figure of the prescription itself (for example, the figure a Standard Maintenance Prescription carries for its early-refill threshold).

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A 30-day dispensing, a patient on a Commercial HMO/EPO Account: 70 percent of 30 is 21 days. The same dispensing for a patient on a Medicaid Managed Care Account: 85 percent of 30 is 25.5 days.
